biography.plain_text: Gerald D. Hines was an American billionaire real-estate developer who founded Houston-based Hines in 1957. A mechanical engineer from a steel-mill family, he built a one-man office into a privately held international investment and development firm. Landmark collaborations with leading architects made commercial design and engineering central to both his fortune and professional legacy.

long_biography.plain_text:
Gerald D. Hines changed commercial development by treating architecture and engineering as operating disciplines, not decoration. He paired One Shell Plaza with Bruce Graham and Fazlur Khan, then worked with Philip Johnson and John Burgee on Pennzoil Place. These projects showed that ambitious design could attract tenants and sustain value through weaker markets.

The Houston developer also reshaped the firm's financing after risking his full net worth on two simultaneous projects. He increasingly recruited institutional equity partners, retaining selected property stakes while earning development and management returns. That structure supported expansion beyond Houston without concentrating every project's risk on his balance sheet. Hines transferred day-to-day leadership to his son Jeff in 1990 while continuing the company's international development from Europe.
